## Complete log-ratio and early-endpoint repair

I re-read the entire new hLogRatio and hEarlyEndpoint, including all guards, algebra and uses, not only their altered tactics.

In hLogRatio, u>0 and u≤v imply v>0 and v-u≥0. The exact pinned log tangent/inverse-tangent bounds yield hDiff and hLower. The new hMiddle explicitly identifies the two copies of the common middle fraction. The ordered calculation now proves

`log(1+v)u = u(log(1+v)-log(1+u)) + u log(1+u)`

`≤ (v-u)u/(1+u) + u log(1+u) ≤ (v-u)log(1+u)+u log(1+u) = log(1+u)v`.

The final positive-denominator comparison is therefore mathematically exact, including u=v. It expresses the same decreasing log-ratio bound needed before the Bennett exponent is negated.

In hEarlyEndpoint, the numerical assumptions and endpoint A=x sqrt(N)/2 are unchanged. The new hA3 compares nonnegative squares explicitly; its square bound follows from A²=x²N/4, x²≥256 and j≤N. hAB0 now supplies the actual sqrt(N)²=N identity after clearing the same positive denominators. The resulting identities remain AB0/j=y/400 and A/(72B0)=(25/18)x². No lower/upper direction or constant changes.

The complete monotonicity/substitution, y≥160000, log(y)≥8, and exponent payment remain the previously reviewed valid proof of `R_j≤(j/N)exp(−2x²)`. The new hInvLog first proves exp(−log y)=y⁻¹ using y>0, then rewrites the intended exponential factor. This removes the prior rewrite-order failure without introducing a new identity or domain assumption. All former empty-strip and j≥x² guards, floors, closed endpoints and support200 conditions remain exact.
